title: Few Clothes' place, the draft, and joining Jack Carey's band
summary: Working in the district, Lee is chased out for lacking a draft registration card and joins Jack Carey's band with Edmund Hall.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: George Few Clothes Place. So Buddy Petit had joined the tuxedo band with Celestan, then went out to the suburban garden. So I goes out to George Few Clothes in the district and work for, and work where Buddy Petit was playing with Jimmy Noon and that bunch. So, that time, there was coming drafting and drafting for the World War I. Registration was coming around. And the guy was looking for, that didn't register for the war, didn't register to go to war. And the guy asked me, say, let me see your registration card. I was a pretty big boy for my age. I was way older than my age because I was tall and slender and had on them big high waist and long pants with my uncle. So I told him, I said, I didn't have no registration card. I said, I'm not old enough to go to war. And then he said, what you doing here? And he said, and he gave me about three minutes, three seconds to get out. So I got out the district, and I joined Jack Kerrie's band. Jack Kerrie's band, a young Clannett player just had come and just began playing with Edmund Hall. And so Jack Kerrie had had his brother playing, cornered with him, Mud Kerrie, so Mud Kerrie had went with Ory, back with Kid Ory's band. So I got in Jack Kerrie's band and told Jack Kerrie about this young Clannett player that I liked. So Jack Kerrie said, get him. And the Clannett player was Edmund Hall. So we worked with Jack Kerrie. And that time Jack Kerrie was playing Tiger Rag, which was not on wax then, but they was calling it Jack Kerrie, playing old Tiger Rag. But we didn't call it Tiger Rag. So they taught me Tiger Rag, and everybody would play Jack Kerrie. So we was playing spot jobs all around Magazine Street, all the rich jobs, fraternity jobs, and everybody was doing good. I was making quite a bit jack for myself at that time, very young, still was in my teens, still was in my teens, playing cornet. So then I stayed with Jack Kerrie's band for about a year. And I leaves Jack Kerrie's band and joined another band called the Young Tuxedo Band.
